title: Grateful Dead Live at Springfield Civic Center on 1985-03-25
lineage: Vault Cassettes (Tascam 122 MKIII) > Dick Latvala's Cassettes (Tascam 122 MKIII); Dick's 1st generation cassettes played back on a Nakamichi Dragon > Panasonic SV-3800 DAT (16/48) by Rob Eaton; Rob Eaton's DAT 16/48 (Panasonic SV-3800) > Tim Dalton's DAT (Panasonic SV-3800)(16/48); Tim Dalton's DAT (16/48)(Sony PCM R-500) > Tascam DA-3000 (DSF 1-bit/5.6 MHz)> .wav (16/48) > Adobe Audition CC 2020 > TLH flac1648
source: Master Vault Cassettes > Dick Latvala's 1st generation cassettes > Rob Eaton's DAT (16/48) > Tim Dalton's DAT (16/48)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with some static and high‑pitched noise, but the show shines thanks to a soaring Sugaree and crisp Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad.
ai_review.review: The performance is highlighted by Jerry Garcia’s soaring guitar on Sugaree and a tight, speedway rendition of Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad, with several other bright spots like Help>Slip>Franklin's. The SBD source sounds decent overall but suffers from noticeable static and a high‑pitched hum that can be tamed with digital filtering. Reviewers are split between praising the musical peaks and critiquing the recording’s imperfections.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is generally good with multiple standout songs, while recording quality is fair due to static and noise issues; weighted average yields a solid mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Marred by static and a high‑pitched noise that detracts from clarity; EQ/BAL needed. Some other source mixes run fast, but the updated SBD (150966) is usable after digital filtering.

standout_songs: Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts sloppy with tech issues on Jack Straw, then peaks with Sugaree and Bird Song. Second set is mixed – bright moments in Help>Slip>Franklin's and Goin' Down the Road, but interrupted by occasional sloppiness and noise.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar soars on Sugaree (4:25 mark) and he quickly picks up Brent’s melody during Bird Song.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as low on Keep Your Day Job.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent adds a melodic line early in Bird Song; keyboards are otherwise solid.
band_member_comments.Drums: The back‑line drives an uptempo Eyes of the World, providing respectable momentum.
